phrases.translation: By the fig and the olive ˹of Jerusalem˺
phrases.text: The commentators differed over what the two are. Most said the fig that is eaten and the olive that is pressed. Some said the fig is the mosque of Damascus and the olive is Jerusalem. Tabari keeps the fruit, because that is what the Arabs know by these names.

Some said this is the mountain of Moses and the place of his prayer. Others said the Tur is any mountain that brings forth crops, and that the word means clean and beautiful. Tabari takes it as the well-known mountain, since the Tur is the mountain with trees and the added word only identifies it.
The city that is safe for its people against their enemies, and the word is used in the sense of the one who is trusted. The commentators agree that Mecca alone is meant.

phrases.translation: Indeed, We created humans in the best form
phrases.text: This is the answer to the oath: by the fig and the olive, We created man in the finest form. The commentators read the words as the most balanced creation and the finest shape, and Tabari keeps them together.
phrases.ar: لَقَدۡ خَلَقۡنَا ٱلۡإِنسَٰنَ فِيٓ أَحۡسَنِ تَقۡوِيمٖ

phrases.translation: But We will reduce them to the lowest of the low ˹in Hell˺
phrases.text: The commentators differed. Some said the most contemptible old age, when the reason departs. Some said the Fire and the worst form in it, even the form of a pig. Tabari takes the old age, because God proves the resurrection by what people see with their own eyes, the change from beauty and strength to weakness and senility.

phrases.translation: except those who believe and do good—
phrases.text: The exception is from the sentence about man, and the commentators explain that the good a believer did while he was strong and well is still recorded for him when old age takes his reason away, and he is not called to account for what he did in that state. Tabari takes this as the soundest reading.

phrases.translation: they will have a never-ending reward
phrases.text: The reward is uncurtailed and undiminished, and it is the same reward they earned while they were able to act.

phrases.translation: Now, what makes you deny the ˹final˺ Judgment
phrases.text: After these proofs, who can still deny you, O Muhammad, the reckoning and the recompense? The commentators agree that mankind is meant, and Tabari says the word for judgment here means the recompense and the settling of accounts.

phrases.translation: Is Allah not the most just of all judges
phrases.text: Is God not wiser than every judge among His servants? The Prophet used to answer yes when he recited this, and Ibn Abbas used to say glory be to You, O God, indeed yes.
